C — Certificate: CHSH → certified bits → seed

Letter folder C_certificate/ of the Quantum Phantoms reverse-engineering epic (epic). Markdown is the source of truth; python -m shared.site.build renders it to site/C_certificate/index.html. Target states live only in status.json (lifecycle: listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected).

Purpose

Make "certified" a number: CHSH value → min-entropy bound H_min ≥ 1 − log₂(1 + √(2 − S²/4)) → certified-bit count → Toeplitz-extracted seed, with hidden test rounds whose choice is seeded from CURBy, and a ledger format modelled on the beacon chain. The extracted seed seeds every PRNG downstream (shared.seedhash.rng).

How to run (sim commands)

All commands run with cwd reverse-engineering/ and the conda base python. Only fetch_pulses uses the network.

# certificate runs → C_certificate/runs/<ts>-chsh-<mode>[-classical]/
python -m C_certificate.src.certify --mode ideal      # simulated: ideal
python -m C_certificate.src.certify --mode heron      # simulated: Heron-class noise (FakeMarrakesh)
python -m C_certificate.src.certify --mode ideal --settings classical   # fail path: S ≤ 2 → rejected + logged
#   options: --rounds 100000 --test-frac 0.2 --pulse-index -1 --eps-est 1e-6 --eps-ext 1e-6 --out-len 256

# reproductions → figures/
python -m C_certificate.repro.pironio        # #4: Pironio 42 bits + H_min-vs-S curve with our latest runs
python -m C_certificate.repro.beacon_chain   # #5: verify cached beacon chain + tamper test

# one-off: refresh the committed pulse cache repro/data/beacon_pulses.json (network)
python -m C_certificate.repro.fetch_pulses --n 12

# check outputs against the frozen contracts
python -m shared.validate C_certificate/runs/<run>/certificate.json C_certificate/runs/<run>/quantum_job_record.json

Run directory contents:

  • run.json, counts_<job>.json;
  • quantum_job_record.json, with counts keyed "xy ab" and test_round_mask as a file_ref;
  • certificate.json;
  • accounting.json, with every number used: Ŝ, E_xy, n_xy, δ_xy, S_low, ε values, h, bits, pulse and circuit hashes;
  • rounds.npz (x, y, a, b, test), test_round_mask.json;
  • extracted.bin (pass only).

Rejections are appended to runs/rejections.jsonl. Runs are deterministic for a given cached pulse and mode: the test mask, the Aer seeds and the Toeplitz seed are all derived from the pulse.

Claim level and honesty notes

L0 only. Simulated CHSH certifies nothing: the deliverable is the accounting pipeline validated on simulated data — every certificate says "certification-ready, not certified (simulated)". S ≤ 2 ⇒ status fail, no seed, draw rejected and logged (no retry, no fallback).

  • Pass/fail rule. Pass requires the lower confidence bound S_low > 2, not only Ŝ > 2. Too little entropy for a 256-bit seed is a second fail reason.
  • Statistical model. The accounting is i.i.d. with Hoeffding finite statistics, not the EAT. It is fine for a pipeline validated on simulated data; a real hardware claim needs an EAT-style bound [C06, C07].
  • The simulator knows the mask. Hidden test rounds only matter against a real device.
  • External seed source. The external pulse is NIST Beacon 2.0, fully verified offline. CURBy [C04] is dissected only: its CIDs are not recomputed, and its latest round (2025-08-22) is flagged isQuantum: False.
  • Not reachable. Liu 2025 [C02] (XEB certified randomness) is an L2-type claim and is read only.

Pipeline readiness

Usable with caveats

C is the only quantum stage that ran inside the chain: four commit → certify prefixes in Heron mode all passed (Ŝ 2.722–2.762, S_low 2.403–2.442, 15 668–17 869 certified bits; C_certificate/runs/20261029-18*-chsh-heron). No chain obtained a beacon pulse later than its commit: NIST /pulse/last lagged 2–3 min and then timed out, so the runner fell back to the cache (beacon_fresh: false). Reusing that pulse reproduced the identical certificate and seed (7dfb4d50…) in two chains with different commits. "Usable with caveats" means inside this simulated pipeline: simulated CHSH certifies nothing.

Future

Shared, pipeline-wide context (end goal, digital-twin path, cross-letter risks) lives once in the whole-pipeline Future. This section covers only what this letter adds. Every claim carries a label: evidence-based (a number in this repo or a cited paper), extrapolation (a reasoned step beyond the evidence), speculative (possible, not supported yet).

1. Aim of the paper(s)

  • [C01] Pironio et al. 2010: randomness certified by a Bell-inequality violation. A CHSH value above 2 bounds how predictable the outputs can be, without trusting the device.
  • [C05] Vazirani–Vidick: "certifiable quantum dice": randomness expansion with untrusted devices.
  • [C02] Liu 2025: certified randomness from random-circuit sampling on a trapped-ion processor (a classical- hardness-based claim; read only here).
  • [C04] Kavuri (CURBy): traceable public random numbers published in a hash-chained beacon.

Why it matters: "random" becomes auditable. You get a number of certified bits with a proof, plus a public timestamp that shows the randomness was not chosen after the fact.

2. Contribution

  • The accounting pipeline reproduced: 40.8 certified bits against Pironio's 42 (−2.8 %). evidence-based
  • A beacon chain verified offline: 11/11 links and 12/12 signatures; a 1-bit edit is caught at its pulse. evidence-based
  • In the INT chain prefix (Heron-class noise): Ŝ 2.722–2.762, S_low 2.403–2.442, 15 668–17 869 certified bits; the S ≤ 2 path is rejected and logged. evidence-based
  • INT findings: no post-commit pulse was obtained (beacon lag), and a reused pulse reproduces the same seed. evidence-based

3. Role in cancer detection

End goal: every synthetic cohort used to train or test a cancer detector carries a certificate proving its random choices were fixed by an external, timestamped source, not hand-picked (no cherry-picking of easy or hard cases after seeing results). This is data credibility for audits and regulators. It does not raise detection accuracy by itself. extrapolation

4. Beyond lungs

  • Any randomized step in medicine: virtual-trial arm assignment, Monte Carlo dose simulation (how the PRNG affects radiotherapy simulations is studied in [E05]), and audit of trial randomization. extrapolation
  • Other synthetic data. MR, pathology and genomics generators need the same "not cherry-picked" guarantee. extrapolation

5. Long-term vision: toward a digital twin

speculative A digital twin runs many stochastic simulations (growth, response, imaging). C's role is to make each one replayable and trustworthy: every random input is traceable to a certified, timestamped source. Path: (1) a simulated certificate + public beacon (now) → (2) a hardware certificate per cohort → (3) device-independent certified randomness as a service that twin platforms call for every simulation batch.

6. Predictions

5 years Assumptions: superconducting hardware without loophole-free conditions; i.i.d. finite statistics; NIST Beacon available.

  • Accounting is validated on simulated data; simulated CHSH certifies nothing. evidence-based
  • Loophole-free Bell tests on superconducting circuits exist in the lab [C03]. Device-independent randomness expansion has been shown with photons [C06]. evidence-based
  • One Heron hardware CHSH run gives a real (not loophole-free) certificate for a small cohort. extrapolation

10 years Assumptions: entropy-accumulation (EAT) finite statistics [C06, C07]; service-grade public beacons.

  • Certified-randomness services become a standard provenance stamp for regulated synthetic datasets. extrapolation

15 years Assumptions: fault-tolerant hardware.

  • speculative Certified randomness from random-circuit sampling at scale [C02], where the guarantee rests on classical hardness (claim level L2), becomes cheap enough to stamp every simulation batch of a twin platform.

Contract change requests

  • CCR-C1: quantum_job_record, multi-circuit jobs.
    • Need: one logical CHSH job runs 4 setting circuits, but transpiled_hash holds one hash.
    • Request: add an optional transpiled_hashes[], one per circuit.
    • Local workaround: transpiled_hash = sha256(canonical_json([4 circuit hashes])). The list is in accounting.json as circuit_hashes. sim_seed is the base Aer seed; setting k (00, 01, 10, 11) uses sim_seed + k.
  • CCR-C2: certificate, recomputable entropy.
    • Need: h_min_per_round = f(S_low), not f(chsh_S), so a consumer cannot recompute it from the certificate.
    • Request: add chsh_S_lower and eps {est, ext}. The validator could then check h = f(chsh_S_lower) and certified_bits = ⌊n_gen · h⌋.
    • Related: the schema caps chsh_S at 2.8285, but a statistical Ŝ can exceed 2√2 (we saw 2.8365 on one ideal run). We clip chsh_S to 2.8284 and keep the raw Ŝ in accounting.json. Consider maximum: 4 (the algebraic CHSH bound).
    • Local workaround: everything is in accounting.json.
  • CCR-C3: certificate.curby_pulse_id, naming. The pulse comes from the NIST Beacon (nist:<chain>:<index>), not CURBy. Consider renaming the field to beacon_pulse_id. Local workaround: the field name is kept, and the value carries the source prefix.
